summary: Heart's Content's red-and-white cast-iron tower of 1901 stands at the harbour entrance; an 1894 tower was sent to Random Head, and the town is known for the 1866 cable.

access.note: Grounds open, tower closed (Lighthouse Friends). Road along the harbour from the north end of town, 1.3 km.

corrections.why: The register (entry 20749) and the Canadian Coast Guard list both give the tower as 8.7 m. The record's 9.1 m has no source among those read.
Lighthouse Friends says the Coast Guard owns the lighthouse. The register copy credits the town only for a photograph, not for ownership. A human should confirm.
Follows from the agency correction above. Needs a human check against current Coast Guard records.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Coast Guard list gives Fl W 4s for the present light and is the official current source; the record's characteristic matches it. Lighthouse Friends gives a fixed red light for the 1901 tower (historic). The Newfoundland 3D gallery's occulting white light every 6 seconds is not supported by the official list, so the story follows the list and reports the disagreement.
The register and Lighthouse Friends both date the present tower to 1901. Lighthouse Friends says the 1894 cast-iron tower went to Motion Island and Random Head, so it is not the tower built in 1901.

notes_for_editor: Sources: the register (two copies), Lighthouse Friends, the Coast Guard List of Lights and one gallery site. Newfoundland was not part of Canada until 1949, so the Canadian Department of Marine reports in the corpus do not cover this station; no corpus hit for Heart's Content was found. Keeper names, dates and terms come from one source, Lighthouse Friends, which in turn cites the Journal of the House of Assembly of Newfoundland and the Encyclopedia of Newfoundland and Labrador (not read). John Warren's dates are printed '1910s 1940s' with the dash missing; read as 1910s to 1940s. 'at least 1912' for Piercey is a documented span, not an end date. Selena Warren (from 1958) has no end date; her connection may be recent, so the story gives only the role and dates the source prints. The three Warrens share a surname; the sources do not say whether they were related, and the story does not say. Storms, wrecks and rescues: no dated event at or near this station was found in the sources read, so that chapter is omitted. The gallery site's occulting 6-second light and 8 nm range conflict with the official list; the record's range of 11.0 nm is not confirmed by any source read (the Coast Guard extract gives no range), so range is left out of facts. Ownership: the record's agency 'Town of Hearts Content' and ownership 'local' are not supported by Lighthouse Friends, which says the Coast Guard owns it (see corrections). Parks Canada's Directory of Federal Heritage Designations page (id 15052) did not render through fetch_text; its statement is the same text as the register copy cited here. The Telegraph Station Museum claim (27 July 1866) is second-hand through Lighthouse Friends' note. Fact-check 2026-10-27: the 1864 remark is Henry Field's, quoted second-hand through Lighthouse Friends (footnote 2). Shape: five chapters for moderate evidence (the guide's table gives two to four); each has sourced material, so none was dropped.
